title: ORION: Exact Canonical-State Supervision for Systematic Generalization in Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2611.27087v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autoregressive Transformers generally fail on out-of-distribution reasoning due to two primary reasons: positional corruption over long sequences and structural state drift across deep execution steps. We introduce ORION, a framework that supervises exact canonical execution states via auxiliary heads to anchor latent trajectories to valid computational manifolds. Across Folding, GridShift, and CLRS-30, a pre-registered 2 x 2 factorial shows that RoPE and ORION address orthogonal axes. RoPE recovers length extrapolation (59.8%), while ORION recovers depth extrapolation (66.7%). Moreover, their combination complementarily achieves strict additive gain in joint length-depth extrapolation, while either method alone offers near satisfactory results. Negative controls confirm that the gain depends strictly on exact canonical alignment; hashed state statistics fail to constrain depth extrapolation.

translated_title: ORION：面向Transformer系统性泛化的精确规范态监督
translated_abstract: 自回归Transformer在分布外推理中普遍失败，主要归因于两个因素：长序列上的位置损坏以及深层执行步骤中的结构性状态漂移。我们提出了ORION，一个通过辅助头对精确规范执行状态进行监督的框架，将潜在轨迹锚定到有效的计算流形上。在Folding、GridShift和CLRS-30基准上，一项预注册的2×2因子实验表明，RoPE和ORION解决的是相互正交的两个维度：RoPE恢复了长度外推能力（59.8%），而ORION恢复了深度外推能力（66.7%）。此外，两者结合在长度-深度联合外推中实现了严格的加性增益，而单独使用任一方法只能取得接近满意的效果。阴性对照实验证实该增益严格依赖于精确的规范对齐；基于哈希的状态统计无法约束深度外推。
tldr: ORION框架通过辅助头监督精确的规范执行状态来恢复Transformer的深度外推能力（66.7%），与解决长度外推的RoPE形成正交互补，二者结合在长度-深度联合外推中实现严格的加性增益。
en_tdlr: ORION supervises exact canonical execution states via auxiliary heads to recover depth extrapolation (66.7%), complementing RoPE's length extrapolation (59.8%), with their combination achieving strict additive gains in joint length-depth generalization.
